units: pixels (x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale assumed
view: Top-down (overhead) view of a straight two-lane road running vertically through the image, sidewalks on both sides. Both cars drive DOWN the image (+y), front of the car pointing down.

camera.evidence: phase correlation of sidewalk strips between consecutive frames: |shift| < 0.05 px/frame, cumulative < 1 px over the clip (scene/camshift.json)
camera.perspective: Nadir-like top view; road plane faces the camera. Car footprints keep a constant pixel size along the whole image (orange car bbox height 555-570 px from y=300 to y=1790), so one px scale holds for the road plane. Tall objects lean outward from the image centre (lamp post shafts, the pedestrian's body: head projects further from the image centre than the feet), so the person's body points are not all on the ground plane.
